identity.name: James Gadson
home_scenes: Los Angeles soul and funk (late 1960s on)
Los Angeles sessions: Motown West, Herbie Hancock, Patrice Rushen (1970s)
identity.summary: One of the most-recorded drummers in R&B. From Kansas City to Los Angeles, the drummer of Charles Wright's Watts 103rd Street Rhythm Band (Do Your Thing, Express Yourself), then with its bassist Melvin Dunlap and arranger Ray Jackson the band on Bill Withers's Still Bill (Use Me, Lean on Me, Kissing My Love, 1972). Through the 1970s on Motown's West Coast records (Marvin Gaye's I Want You, Diana Ross's Love Hangover, Thelma Houston's Don't Leave Me This Way), Herbie Hancock, Patrice Rushen, Freddie King and B.B. King; later Paul McCartney, Beck, D'Angelo and Vulfpeck. A light hand and damped drums, the hats in 16ths, the kick and the snare or the rim click trading the spaces between them, the time 'in the cracks' between straight and swung (Drummer Cafe). He died in April 2026.

evidence.note: The kick 'unwavering', the hats and rim clicks a fraction either side of it (Melodics, excerpt).

swing.notes: 'In the cracks', very close to straight (Drummer Cafe, Use Me); 'half-swing 16ths' on Kissing My Love and swung 16ths on Lonely Town, Lonely Street (Bishop). Estimates.

dynamics.balance: Even and light: 'not too strong on the accents', the open hat 'just a little sizzle' (Bishop).

feel_profile.interaction: A groove for the song: a different one on each track of Still Bill, the fills building the groove rather than leaving it (Bishop, of Shout It Out).

hand_techniques.name: Cross-stick backbeat
hand_techniques.description: Use Me's rim click on 2 and 4 and in 16ths between the kicks; Running Away's verse on the kick and the rim alone.

hand_techniques.name: 16ths on the hats
hand_techniques.description: Hand to hand, accented lightly on 2 and 4 or on their "and"s.

hand_techniques.name: Open hat on the off-beats
hand_techniques.description: Half-open, 'a little sizzle', on the "e" and "a" at the end of a bar (Use Me) or on 4 (Shout It Out).

hand_techniques.name: Even 16th fills
hand_techniques.description: Fills 'at an even volume and ... right on the 16th note pulse', round two concert toms (Shout It Out).

foot_techniques.name: The kick in 16ths between the hands
foot_techniques.description: 'Linear, quasi-paradiddle figures between the Snare (cross-stick) and Kick drum' (Use Me).

coordination.notes: The hats as the ostinato, the kick and the rim or snare talking between.

searched: Todd Bishop's Still Bill grooves, Use Me breaks and Shout It Out (34 bars)
devices_search.note: No device found: the one displacement is the backbeat moved a 16th to the "e" of 2 in Shout It Out, a groove rather than a device.

voice_language.hihat: 16ths, hand to hand, lightly accented; half-open on the off-beats; eighths on some songs.
voice_language.snare: A cross-stick on Use Me and Running Away, the snare elsewhere; ghosts few and light.
voice_language.kick: Steady and talking: 16ths between the hands on Use Me, a Motown pattern on Running Away.
voice_language.toms: In fills; a rack-tom accent on the "and" of 4 (Running Away); the floor tom with a mallet (I Don't Know).
voice_language.cymbals: A crash at the end of a fill, sometimes on the last 16th, tied over the bar line.

implements.notes: A mallet on the floor tom and brushes overdubbed on I Don't Know (Bishop).

sound_profile.cymbal_character: Small, quiet hats; the open hat a sizzle rather than a wash.

sample_hints.soul: A damped 1960s kit, a short fat snare and a woody rim click, the toms under towels.

signature_traits.label: The rim and the kick in 16ths
signature_traits.description: Use Me: a cross-stick on 2 and 4 and in the spaces, the kick filling the 16ths between, under even hats.

signature_traits.label: In the cracks
signature_traits.description: 16ths between straight and swung, nearer straight on Use Me, half-swung on Kissing My Love.

signature_traits.label: Drums under towels
signature_traits.description: The snare and toms damped, dry and warm, the open hat only a sizzle.

patterns.name: Use Me: the rim and the kick in 16ths
patterns.function: Sixteenths on the hats, a cross-stick on 2 and 4, the kick on 1, its "and", the "e" and "a" of 2, 3, its "and" and "a", the "e" and "a" of 4; in the second bar no rim on 4, the hat opened on the "e" and "a" of 3 and the "e" of 4.

patterns.name: Kissing My Love: the record's opening groove
patterns.function: Half-swung 16ths on the hats accented on 2 and 4, the foot and the kick on 1, the snare on 2 and 4, a ghost on the "e" of 3, the kick on the "a" of 3 and the "and" of 4; then a ghost on the "a" of 2 as well, the kick on the "e" of 4 and the hat opened on its "and".

patterns.name: Shout It Out: the backbeat on the "e" of 2
patterns.function: The hat on the beats, closed on 1 and opened on 4; the snare on the "e" of 2 and on 4; the kick on 1, the "a" of 1, the "a" of 2 and 3.

patterns.name: Running Away: the rim click and no hat
patterns.function: The kick in a Motown pattern (1, its "and", the "a" of 2, 3 and its "and"), a rim click on 2 and 4, the rack tom on the "and" of 4; no hat.
